candidates.attacker_control: The full XML document body supplied to a public read API (e.g. XmlMapper.readValue(InputStream/String, Class), readTree, or XmlFactory.createParser): the attacker controls the prolog DOCTYPE, internal/external entity declarations, and entity references in element/attribute content. No framework internals need to be controlled.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked every file for any DTD/entity hardening: no SUPPORT_DTD, IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, XMLConstants, XMLResolver, or SecurityManager usage exists in the snapshot; the only setProperty calls are XMLOutputFactory.IS_REPAIRING_NAMESPACES and XMLInputFactory.IS_COALESCING (XmlFactory.java:139-141). XmlMapper's default constructor and the README's canonical 'new XmlMapper()' usage both reach this default path. Countervailing factors: callers who pass their own XMLInputFactory (XmlFactory(XMLInputFactory)/setXMLInputFactory) or who use Woodstox (external entities default false) may be unaffected; FromXmlParser.Feature is empty, so there is no module-level toggle either way. No tests or runtime experiments were available in scope.
candidates.impact: Parsing attacker-controlled XML can perform XML External Entity attacks: reading local files via file:// system entities into deserialized values/error diagnostics, SSRF by fetching attacker-chosen http(s) URLs referenced from external entities/DTD, and denial of service via recursive entity expansion. This matches the known class of XXE/SSRF flaw for which upstream later added explicit SUPPORT_DTD=false / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false in _initFactories. Impact is provider-dependent and was not executed or runtime-verified here.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses the default XmlFactory()/XmlMapper() (no pre-configured, hardened XMLInputFactory) to parse untrusted XML, and the StAX implementation in use enables DTD processing and external entity resolution by default. The JDK's built-in StAX (used when Woodstox is absent; woodstox-core is only a test-scope dependency in pom.xml) is the notable case where isSupportingExternalEntities/supportDTD defaults permit external resolution. With Woodstox, external entities default off, which partially mitigates SSRF/file reads but not internal DTD/entity processing.
candidates.root_cause: XmlFactory wires the StAX reader to a bare XMLInputFactory obtained from XMLInputFactory.newInstance() (or supplied by the caller) and its _initFactories() hardening only enables namespace repair on the writer and IS_COALESCING on the reader. No SUPPORT_DTD=false, no IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false, and no restrictive XMLResolver is ever applied, and FromXmlParser.Feature contains no option to disable DTD/entity handling. As a result, XmlMapper's default read path processes DOCTYPE declarations and external entity references according to provider defaults.
candidates.title: Default XmlFactory/XmlMapper parsing does not disable DTD processing or external entities (XXE/SSRF)
candidates.trace: new XmlMapper() -> new XmlFactory() -> xmlIn = XMLInputFactory.newInstance() (XmlFactory.java:113) -> _initFactories() sets only IS_COALESCING (XmlFactory.java:141). readValue(...) -> ObjectMapper read path -> XmlFactory._createParser(InputStream|Reader) -> _xmlInputFactory.createXMLStreamReader(in|r) (XmlFactory.java:536/554) -> _initializeXmlReader() calls sr.next() in a loop until START_ELEMENT (XmlFactory.java:648), which forces the parser through the prolog DOCTYPE before the root element. Any external entity reference is resolved by the provider's default XMLResolver; expanded content reaches the databind layer as ordinary text/attribute values (XmlTokenStream._collectUntilTag / FromXmlParser), or the request-side effect (URL fetch) happens inside the StAX parser. Repo-wide searches for SUPPORT_DTD, EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, Resolver, Security returned no hardening anywhere.
candidates.unverified: Runtime exploitability depends on the StAX provider selected by XMLInputFactory.newInstance() in the deployment classpath; the actual default values of SUPPORT_DTD and IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES for the provider in use were not verified by execution. No runtime reproduction, payload execution, or external service access was performed; file disclosure/SSRF/DoS behavior is inferred from source and API semantics.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (leads to CWE-918 SSRF and file disclosure)

coverage_summary: All 39 repository files under the assigned source root were listed (34 Java main sources, pom.xml, README.md, .travis.yml, .gitignore); no files were filtered by the safety/exclusion rules (excluded_over_5_mib=0, excluded_sensitive_name_or_path=0, excluded_symlinks=0). Fully read: XmlFactory.java, XmlMapper.java, XmlTokenStream.java, XmlBeanDeserializerModifier.java, XmlTypeResolverBuilder.java, StaxUtil.java, JacksonXmlModule.java, XmlAnnotationIntrospector.java, XmlJaxbAnnotationIntrospector.java, pom.xml (imports/deps), and document sections of README.md. Read substantial portions of FromXmlParser.java and ToXmlGenerator.java, and performed repo-wide literal searches for DTD, entit(y|ies), SUPPORT_DTD, EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, setProperty, Resolver, Security, Class.forName, readObject, Runtime, URL, writeRaw, and related APIs. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: full bodies of ToXmlGenerator (1141 lines), DefaultXmlPrettyPrinter, XmlSerializerProvider, serializer/deserializer helper classes, annotation interfaces, and util classes beyond targeted searches.
limitations: No test sources or runtime harness are present in the snapshot; no execution, scanning, or exploit reproduction was performed, so the finding remains a source-evidence lead.

The decisive behavioral factor (whether the deployment's StAX provider enables DTD/external entities by default) cannot be determined from this repository because the provider is chosen at runtime via XMLInputFactory.newInstance(); woodstox-core is only a test-scope dependency in pom.xml.
No upstream diff, patch, CVE advisory, or ground-truth data was consulted (per review constraints), so the exact fixed-version correspondence was not verified from the snapshot itself.
Line-by-line review of the large serializer/pretty-printer classes was partial; residual issues there are possible but no concrete evidence was found.

rejected_leads.lead: XmlFactory JDK-serialization path instantiates classes by name: readObject stores _jdkXmlInFactory/_jdkXmlOutFactory and readResolve does Class.forName(...).newInstance() (XmlFactory.java:183-224).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an attacker to already control a serialized XmlFactory object fed to ObjectInputStream (not reachable from the XML parsing path), and needs a suitable no-arg-constructor XMLInputFactory/XMLOutputFactory class on the classpath to be dangerous; weaker and more conditional than the XXE lead.

rejected_leads.lead: XmlTypeResolverBuilder/XmlClassNameIdResolver decode attacker-supplied class names when polymorphic type info is used (XmlTypeResolverBuilder.java:115-166).
rejected_leads.reason: Only active if the application explicitly enables default typing or @JsonTypeInfo(Id.CLASS/MINIMAL_CLASS); the module merely encodes '..' for XML names. The trust decision belongs to databind's polymorphic-deserialization configuration, not a distinct root cause in this repository snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: ToXmlGenerator raw output and element/attribute name handling (writeRaw, writeStartElement, writeFieldName).
rejected_leads.reason: Element/attribute values are escaped by the StAX writer and names come from POJO/type metadata, not directly from parsed input; writeRaw is a developer-facing pass-through. No attacker-controlled path to unescaped markup was identified.
Malformed/empty/comment-only documents terminate via XMLStreamException or end-of-document handling; no unbounded loop or resource leak was demonstrated from source.

summary: Reviewed the jackson-dataformat-xml 2.7.4-SNAPSHOT snapshot (39 files: main sources, pom, README, build files). The strongest plausible issue is the missing XML external-entity hardening in the default XmlFactory/XmlMapper parsing path: XmlFactory creates the StAX XMLInputFactory via XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and only sets IS_COALESCING, never disabling DTD support or external entity resolution, and there is no library-level feature to opt out. Parsing any attacker-supplied XML through XmlMapper.readValue()/readTree() therefore inherits whatever the provider defaults are; with implementations that enable DTDs and external entities by default (e.g., the JDK built-in StAX), this yields XXE-driven local file disclosure, SSRF to internal endpoints, and entity-expansion DoS. This is a lead based on source evidence, not a runtime-confirmed exploit.
